# 12-Week Postpartum Return-to-Fitness Programme

**Client profile:** 33-year-old female, 4 weeks post uncomplicated C-section, OB-cleared for light activity only until 6-week check, home training with yoga mat only.

**Core principles across the programme:**
- Rebuild deep core and pelvic floor function before loading
- Respect scar healing — the C-section scar is fascia and muscle, not just skin, and takes 6–12 months to fully remodel
- Screen for diastasis recti (DRA) before any progression into loaded core work; coning/doming is a red flag to regress
- Breath-led movement: exhale on effort, inhale to relax
- No breath-holding, no bearing down, no jumping until Week 5 of the programme at the earliest (and only after 6-week clearance)
- Bleeding heavier or brighter, pelvic heaviness, leaking, or scar pain = regress immediately

---

## PHASE 1 — Reconnect & Restore (Weeks 1–2)
*Pre-6-week check. Light activity only.*

**Weekly structure:** 6 days/week, 15–25 minutes. Daily walking on top.

### Week 1

**Daily (7 days):** Diaphragmatic breathing, 2 sets of 10 breaths, morning and evening. Lying on back, knees bent, one hand on ribs, one on belly. Inhale wide into ribs, exhale slow through pursed lips feeling gentle natural lift of pelvic floor and drawing in of lower belly. No forcing.

**Sessions (Mon/Wed/Fri):** 15 min
- Connection breathing — 2 × 10 breaths
- Pelvic floor contractions (Kegels) — 2 × 10 slow (5s hold, 5s release) + 2 × 10 quick pulses
- Heel slides — 2 × 8 each leg
- Pelvic tilts — 2 × 10
- Glute squeezes supine — 2 × 10 (5s hold)
- Scar mobilisation: once scar is fully healed and cleared, light fingertip circles around (not on) the scar for 2–3 min

**Tues/Thurs/Sat:** 20–30 min flat walking at conversational pace.

**Sun:** Rest or gentle walk.

### Week 2
Same structure, add:
- Side-lying clam — 2 × 10 each
- Supine marching (single leg lift, keeping pelvis neutral) — 2 × 8 each
- Cat-cow — 2 × 8, gentle
- Bird-dog *arm only* and *leg only* (not combined yet) — 2 × 6 each side
- Walks progress to 25–35 min

---

## PHASE 2 — Foundation (Weeks 3–4)
*Assumes 6-week OB check passed with clearance for more. If not cleared, hold in Phase 1.*

**DRA check at start of Week 3.** Supine, knees bent, small head/shoulder lift, palpate along linea alba above, at, and below navel. Note gap width (fingers) and depth/tension. Any gap >2 fingers with poor tension = keep core work regressive, no crunching-pattern movements.

**Weekly structure:** 4 strength sessions + walking.

### Week 3 & 4 — Full-body foundational (Mon/Wed/Fri) — 25–30 min

Warm-up: cat-cow ×8, glute bridge ×10, world's greatest stretch ×3/side

Circuit — 3 rounds:
1. Bodyweight box squat to mat/couch height — 10 reps
2. Incline push-up against wall — 8–10 reps
3. Glute bridge — 12 reps, 2s pause at top
4. Bird-dog (full, opposite arm/leg) — 6 each side, slow
5. Side-lying clam — 12 each
6. Dead bug with heel taps (no lumbar arching) — 6 each side
7. Standing single-leg balance — 20s each

**Tues/Thurs:** Walk 30–40 min + mobility flow 10 min
**Sat:** Optional yoga-style mobility session (avoid deep twists, deep backbends, planks)
**Sun:** Rest

Add exhale-on-effort cueing to every rep. Watch for doming through core work.

---

## PHASE 3 — Build Capacity (Weeks 5–7)

Reassess DRA at Week 5. Introduce short holds, longer levers, and controlled loading through bodyweight variations. Still no jumping unless DRA closed to <2 fingers with good tension, no leaking, no heaviness.

**Weekly structure:** 4 sessions, 30–35 min.

### Week 5 — Upper/Lower Split

**Mon — Lower body**
- Bodyweight squat — 3 × 12
- Reverse lunge — 3 × 8 each
- Single-leg glute bridge — 3 × 8 each
- Side-lying hip abduction — 3 × 12 each
- Calf raise — 3 × 15

**Tues** — Walk 35–45 min

**Wed — Upper body & core**
- Incline push-up (lower angle: mat edge on stairs/sofa) — 3 × 8
- Prone Y-T-W raises — 2 × 8 each
- Superman hold — 3 × 15s
- Dead bug — 3 × 8 each side
- Side plank from knees — 3 × 15s each
- Bird-dog — 3 × 8 each

**Thurs** — Walk + mobility

**Fri — Full body**
- Squat to reach — 3 × 12
- Push-up (incline) — 3 × 8
- Reverse lunge — 3 × 8 each
- Wall sit — 3 × 20s
- Bird-dog — 3 × 8 each

**Sat** — Longer walk 45 min or gentle yoga
**Sun** — Rest

### Week 6
Same structure, add reps (+2), add 5s to isometrics, deepen squat range if comfortable.

### Week 7
- Progress push-ups to lower incline (bench height)
- Introduce split squat (static lunge) 3 × 8 each
- Side plank from knees → progress to 25s
- Add pallof-style anti-rotation using a resistance band anchored around a door hinge, *if* she can source one — 3 × 8 each. Otherwise, standing chops with a light water bottle.

---

## PHASE 4 — Strengthen & Integrate (Weeks 8–10)

Client should now be ~14 weeks postpartum. Ready for more challenging bodyweight strength and, if DRA and pelvic floor are good, low-impact plyometric prep.

**Weekly structure:** 4 sessions + walking, 35–40 min.

### Week 8

**Mon — Lower**
- Bulgarian split squat (rear foot on mat/low surface) — 3 × 8 each
- Single-leg glute bridge — 3 × 10 each
- Sumo squat — 3 × 12
- Curtsy lunge — 3 × 8 each
- Calf raise, single leg — 3 × 10 each

**Wed — Upper/core**
- Push-up, knees (or full if strong) — 3 × 6–8
- Pike push-up from knees — 2 × 6
- Side plank full — 3 × 20s each
- Dead bug with arm extension — 3 × 8 each
- Bird-dog with 2s pause — 3 × 8 each
- Hollow hold — 3 × 15s (regress to bent-knee if any doming)

**Fri — Full body conditioning**
- Squat — 15 reps
- Push-up — max quality reps
- Reverse lunge — 10 each
- Glute bridge — 15
- Side plank — 20s each
40s work / 20s rest, 3 rounds

**Walking days remain.**

### Week 9
- Progress push-ups toward full range
- Introduce **step-ups** onto a sturdy surface — 3 × 8 each
- Introduce **low-impact "jump prep"**: fast bodyweight squats and heel-lifted squats. Actual jumping only if pelvic floor is asymptomatic on impact test (light bounces in place, no leaking, no heaviness).

### Week 10
- Add tempo squats 3-1-1 — 3 × 10
- Push-up 3 × 8, aim for full push-up if progression allows
- Reverse lunge with knee drive (control, no hop) — 3 × 8 each
- Side plank with hip dip — 3 × 8 each
- If impact-cleared: 2 × 20s low pogo hops, monitor closely

---

## PHASE 5 — Return to Performance (Weeks 11–12)

Client is ~16–18 weeks postpartum. Focus: consolidate strength, layer conditioning, prep her for what's next (loaded lifting, gym return, or running).

### Week 11 — 4 sessions, 40 min

**Mon — Lower strength**
- Bulgarian split squat — 4 × 8 each
- Single-leg RDL (bodyweight) — 3 × 8 each
- Squat jumps (if cleared) 3 × 6, OR tempo squat 3 × 12
- Glute bridge march — 3 × 10 each
- Side-lying abduction — 3 × 15 each

**Tues** — Walk 45–60 min briskly, include short faster intervals

**Wed — Upper/core**
- Full push-up — 4 × max quality
- Pike push-up — 3 × 8
- Side plank full — 3 × 30s each
- Dead bug — 3 × 10 each
- Hollow hold — 3 × 20s
- Bird-dog — 3 × 10 each

**Thurs** — Walk + mobility

**Fri — Conditioning circuit** (40s on / 20s off, 4 rounds)
- Squats
- Push-ups
- Reverse lunges
- Mountain climbers, slow (regress to bird-dog if doming)
- Side plank

**Sat** — Long walk or introduce **walk-jog intervals** if pelvic floor asymptomatic: 4 min walk / 1 min slow jog × 4. If ANY leaking, heaviness, scar tugging, or lower back pain — regress and refer to pelvic floor physio.

### Week 12
Same layout, add load:
- Split squat 4 × 10 each
- Full push-up 4 × 8
- Single-leg RDL 4 × 10
- Walk-jog intervals: 3 min walk / 2 min jog × 5, if asymptomatic

End-of-programme reassessment:
- Repeat DRA test
- Pelvic floor symptom check (leaking, heaviness, pain)
- Scar mobility and sensation
- Movement quality: single-leg squat, push-up, plank hold
- Set next goals: return to loaded lifting, running programme, or higher-intensity training

---

## Recovery & Lifestyle Guidance Throughout

**Sleep:** Almost certainly disrupted. Emphasise she takes rest days seriously and naps opportunistically. If sleep is poor, hold progressions rather than push.

**Hydration:** Especially critical if breastfeeding — aim 2.5–3L/day.

**Nutrition (broad guidance — refer out for specifics):**
- Adequate protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg bodyweight to support tissue recovery and lean mass
- Do not restrict calories aggressively. If breastfeeding, add ~400–500 kcal above maintenance
- Iron, omega-3s, and vitamin D are commonly low postpartum — encourage GP bloodwork if not already done
- Whole-food focus; enough carbs to fuel training and mood

**Scar care:** Once fully healed and OB-cleared, daily massage in circles, then across, then along the scar — 2–3 min. Improves fascial glide and reduces adhesions that pull on core function.

**Red flags to stop and refer:**
- Leaking urine or stool
- Pelvic heaviness or a "bulging" sensation
- Bleeding that becomes heavier or bright red after activity
- Scar pain, pulling, or opening
- Persistent DRA >2 fingers with soft/doughy tension by Week 8
- Lower back or pubic pain

**Strong recommendation:** Get her a one-off appointment with a **pelvic health physiotherapist** early in the programme, ideally around Week 3–4. It's the single highest-ROI intervention for postpartum return and will de-risk everything you do with her.

# Breastfeeding Nutrition Plan — 12-Week Integration

**Important caveats up front:** You're a personal trainer, not a dietitian. This is educational guidance to support her training. For specific meal planning, allergies, or if she has gestational diabetes history, thyroid issues, or postpartum depression, refer to a registered dietitian — ideally one specialising in postpartum/lactation. Also flag that breastfeeding is not the time for aggressive fat loss; slow, sustainable change protects milk supply and her recovery.

---

## Core Principles

**1. Energy needs are elevated.**
Exclusive breastfeeding costs roughly **450–500 kcal/day** above her maintenance. Partial/combination feeding is proportionally less (estimate ~300 kcal/day if mixed feeding). She should eat to hunger — postpartum hunger is real biology, not a lack of discipline.

**2. Don't diet in the first 6–8 weeks postpartum, and go gently thereafter.**
Milk supply is being established until roughly 12 weeks. Sharp calorie deficits (>500 kcal below need) can reduce supply. If fat loss is a goal, wait until Week 6+ of the programme (~10 weeks postpartum), then aim for a modest deficit of 200–300 kcal only, with a supply-first mindset.

**3. Protein, protein, protein.**
Target **1.8–2.2 g/kg bodyweight/day.** Breastfeeding raises protein needs above pregnancy levels, and she's simultaneously rebuilding tissue and training. This is the single most important nutritional lever.

**4. Hydration is non-negotiable.**
Aim **3–3.5 litres/day** from fluids and food. A common practical cue: drink a full glass every time she sits down to feed. Thirst spikes hard during letdown — have water within arm's reach at every feeding station.

**5. Frequent, easy meals beat perfect meals.**
She has a newborn. Structure around 3 meals + 2–3 snacks, with an emphasis on **one-handed, no-prep options** she can eat while feeding.

---

## Daily Targets

| Nutrient | Target | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Calories | Maintenance + 450–500 (EBF) | Milk production cost |
| Protein | 1.8–2.2 g/kg | Tissue repair, satiety, lean mass |
| Carbs | 4–5 g/kg minimum | Milk supply, mood, training energy, brain fuel |
| Fat | 0.8–1.0 g/kg | Hormones, fat-soluble vitamins, DHA in milk |
| Fluids | 3–3.5 L | Milk is ~87% water |
| Fibre | 25–30 g | Constipation is common postpartum |

**Rough example for a 65 kg client:** ~2,300–2,500 kcal, ~130 g protein, ~280 g carbs, ~65 g fat.

## Priority Micronutrients While Breastfeeding

These are commonly under-consumed and matter for both her and baby:

- **Choline** — 550 mg/day. Eggs (yolks!), liver, fish, edamame. Critical for infant brain development, most women under-consume.
- **Iodine** — 290 mcg/day. Dairy, eggs, seafood, iodised salt. Most postnatal vitamins include it — check hers does.
- **DHA (omega-3)** — 200–300 mg/day. Oily fish 2–3×/week (salmon, sardines, mackerel) or an algae/fish oil supplement. Directly influences milk DHA content.
- **Iron** — 9 mg/day while EBF (lower than pregnancy but stores may be depleted). Red meat, lentils, spinach with vitamin C.
- **Calcium** — 1,000 mg/day. Dairy, fortified plant milks, sardines with bones, greens.
- **Vitamin D** — 600 IU minimum; many need 1,000–2,000 IU. Also relevant because most breastfed babies are supplemented directly.
- **B12** — especially critical if she eats plant-based.
- **Zinc** — 12 mg/day. Meat, shellfish, seeds, legumes.

**Continue the prenatal/postnatal multivitamin throughout breastfeeding** as a safety net. It doesn't replace food but covers gaps on hard days.

---

## Foods That Support Milk Supply

There's more folklore than evidence here, but consistent hydration, adequate calories, and adequate carbs are the real drivers. That said, the following are nutrient-dense and traditionally associated with supply support:

- Oats (any form)
- Barley and other whole grains
- Flaxseeds and chia (also fibre + omega-3)
- Fennel, fenugreek — evidence weak, some women swear by them, fenugreek can lower blood sugar so caution
- Brewer's yeast
- Salmon and sardines
- Dark leafy greens
- Eggs
- Full-fat Greek yoghurt

**Foods to moderate but not eliminate:**
- **Caffeine** — up to 300 mg/day (roughly 2 coffees) is considered safe. Time before feeds if baby seems sensitive.
- **Alcohol** — occasional single drink is fine; time so peak blood alcohol (30–60 min after) doesn't coincide with a feed. "Pump and dump" is unnecessary — alcohol clears milk as it clears blood.
- **High-mercury fish** — limit swordfish, king mackerel, shark, tilefish. Salmon, sardines, tinned light tuna are fine.

## Daily Structure

**On waking:** Large glass of water. Prenatal vitamin with food.

**Breakfast (within 60 min of waking):** Protein + carb + fat. E.g., 3-egg scramble with spinach + oats with berries + full-fat yoghurt. ~600 kcal, 35g protein.

**Mid-morning snack:** E.g., Greek yoghurt with granola and flaxseed, or overnight oats. ~300 kcal.

**Lunch:** Palm-sized protein + 2 cupped hands of carbs + vegetables + fat source. E.g., chicken thighs, rice, avocado, roasted veg. ~600 kcal, 40g protein.

**Afternoon snack:** E.g., cottage cheese with fruit, apple with peanut butter, or a protein shake with banana. ~300 kcal.

**Dinner:** Similar template to lunch. Oily fish 2–3×/week ideal. ~600 kcal.

**Evening (if breastfeeding overnight):** A small snack before bed prevents 3am ravenous wake-ups. Toast with nut butter, or milk with oats. ~200 kcal.

## Integration with the 12-Week Programme

### Phase 1 (Weeks 1–2) — Reconnect & Restore
**Focus: Eat abundantly. Do not restrict.**
- Maintenance + 500 kcal daily
- Protein at every meal and snack, 25–30 g per sitting
- Hydration front and centre — a bottle at every feeding spot
- Iron-rich foods 5+ days/week to help replenish blood loss from delivery
- Ask her to get bloodwork if not already done: ferritin, vitamin D, B12, thyroid

### Phase 2 (Weeks 3–4) — Foundation
**Focus: Consistency and habit.**
- Same intake targets
- Add a **pre-training snack** on training days: 20–30 g carbs + small protein 30–45 min before session (banana + Greek yoghurt, toast + egg)
- **Post-training:** Aim to eat within 60 min — a full meal is ideal, or a protein shake + fruit if a meal isn't near
- Track hydration for one week using a marked bottle so she knows her actual intake

### Phase 3 (Weeks 5–7) — Build Capacity
**Focus: Fuel the training load.**
- Training sessions are longer and harder — carbs matter more
- Add 20–30 g carbs to pre- and post-training meals on session days
- If she reports fatigue, mood dips, or supply changes: eat more, especially carbs
- **Do not drop calories here even if fat loss is a goal.** Body composition changes will come from training + protein.

### Phase 4 (Weeks 8–10) — Strengthen & Integrate
**Focus: Optional, modest fat loss if desired and supply is robust.**
- Only if she raises it as a goal AND supply is well-established AND baby is gaining well
- Reduce by only **200–300 kcal/day**, primarily from discretionary foods (alcohol, processed snacks)
- **Never reduce protein.** Protein stays at 1.8–2.2 g/kg.
- Keep at least 200 g carbs/day minimum
- Monitor supply weekly — if pumping output drops, nappy count drops, or baby seems less satisfied, return to maintenance immediately
- Weight loss target: no more than **0.5 kg/week**. Faster than this risks supply and releases fat-stored toxins into milk

### Phase 5 (Weeks 11–12) — Return to Performance
**Focus: Performance nutrition.**
- If doing walk-jog intervals or higher-intensity conditioning, carbs pre-session become important
- Maintain protein at 2.0 g/kg
- If her energy is dipping in sessions, that's a fuelling issue, not a training issue — add carbs before addressing programming
- Discuss longer-term goals: continued breastfeeding, weaning timeline, and how nutrition will shift accordingly

- Persistent fatigue beyond expected newborn tiredness (think anaemia, thyroid, low ferritin)
- Mood symptoms — low mood, anxiety, intrusive thoughts (postpartum depression/anxiety screening)
- Hair loss beyond typical postpartum shedding at 3–4 months
- Persistent constipation despite fibre and fluids
- Signs of disordered eating patterns or excessive restriction
- Rapid weight loss (>1 kg/week) — this can affect supply and indicates under-fuelling

# Progressive Strength Loading — Weeks 1–7 Overlay

The original programme was intentionally conservative through the early phases because the client has no equipment beyond a yoga mat and is early postpartum. Here's how to layer in genuine strength progression from the start, using bodyweight mechanics, tempo, leverage, and range of motion as the loading variables. If she can acquire even a couple of resistance bands and/or a pair of dumbbells (5 kg and 8–10 kg to start), the progressions accelerate meaningfully — I've flagged where equipment additions would help.

**Loading principles being applied:**
- **Tempo** (slower eccentrics, pauses) — the safest way to add difficulty postpartum without adding load
- **Leverage** (single-limb, longer levers, deficit range) — massively increases demand from bodyweight
- **Range of motion** — progressing depth as pelvic floor and core tolerate
- **Density** (reps/time under tension) — before adding reps, add quality time
- **Load** (bands, dumbbells, weighted objects) — introduced cautiously once pelvic floor and core are demonstrably competent

**Non-negotiable gating:** Any progression is contingent on no coning/doming, no leaking, no pelvic heaviness, no scar pain, and clean breath mechanics (exhale on effort). If any of these appear, regress one step.

---

## PHASE 1 — Reconnect & Restore (Weeks 1–2)

**Strength reality check:** She's 4 weeks post-major-abdominal-surgery. "Strength work" here is neuromuscular reconnection, not hypertrophy or load. But we can absolutely make it deliberate and progressive.

### Week 1 — Added strength emphasis

Keep the existing session structure. **Add tempo and holds** to the movements already prescribed:

- **Glute squeezes supine** — progress from 2 × 10 (5s hold) to 2 × 10 (**8s hold with full exhale**). This is a real isometric.
- **Heel slides** — add a 2-second pause at end range. 2 × 8 each leg with 2s pause.
- **Pelvic tilts** — 2 × 10 with a 3-second hold in posterior tilt on each rep.
- **Wall push** (new): Standing, palms against wall at shoulder height. Push into wall with straight arms, exhale, hold 10s. 3 × 10s. This gently loads shoulders, chest, and serratus without any core demand.
- **Wall sit, shallow** (new, end of Week 1 if comfortable): Feet well out from wall, only descend 20–30°. 2 × 15s. Builds quad/glute tolerance.

### Week 2 — Introduce load tolerance

- **Glute bridge** — 3 × 10 with **3s hold at top**, full exhale on the way up
- **Wall sit** — 3 × 20–25s, deeper if comfortable
- **Wall push-up** — 3 × 10 with a **2-second lowering phase**
- **Side-lying clam** — 3 × 10 with a 2s hold at top each side
- **Supine march** — 3 × 8 each leg, slow and controlled
- **Bird-dog (single limb)** — 3 × 6 each, 3-second holds at extension

**What she's actually training:** Motor control, tendon and connective tissue loading, glute and shoulder capacity, and the exhale-brace pattern that everything else will be built on. This is real work.

---

## PHASE 2 — Foundation (Weeks 3–4)

Post 6-week check assumed. Now we introduce **structured strength sessions with progressive overload built in.**

### Week 3 — Strength session template (Mon/Wed/Fri)

Warm-up as previously prescribed, then:

**A1. Box squat to sofa/mat height** — 3 × 10
- Tempo: 3s down, 1s pause on sofa, 1s up
- Progression cue: Depth of surface she's sitting to. Start at sofa height (~45 cm), aim to lower it week by week.

**A2. Incline push-up against wall** — 3 × 8
- Tempo: 3s down, 1s pause, 1s up
- Progression: When 3 × 10 at this tempo feels controlled, move to a lower incline (kitchen counter → sofa arm → coffee table)

**B1. Glute bridge with 3s hold at top** — 3 × 12
- Progression: Add reps to 15, then move to single-leg glute bridge (start with 3 × 6 each)

**B2. Bird-dog full** — 3 × 6 each side
- Tempo: 3s hold at extension, slow return
- Progression: Add reps to 10 each side

**C1. Side-lying clam** — 3 × 12 each, 2s hold
- Progression: **Add a mini-band above knees** if available (this is the single most useful equipment purchase for postpartum glute work)

**C2. Dead bug** — 3 × 6 each side
- Tempo: 3s to extend, 3s to return
- Progression: Full opposite arm/leg dead bug when heel-tap version is clean

**D. Standing single-leg balance** — 3 × 30s each

### Week 4 — Progression targets

- Squat: sofa arm → coffee table height, still 3 × 10 with 3s eccentric
- Push-up: increase reps to 3 × 10 at wall, OR move to counter height at 3 × 8
- Glute bridge: progress to single-leg 3 × 6 each if double-leg feels easy
- Bird-dog: 3 × 8 each with 3s hold
- Dead bug: full opposite limb version, 3 × 8 each
- Add: **Split stance balance work** — staggered stance holds, 3 × 20s each side, prep for lunging

**Equipment addition worth suggesting:** A pair of mini-bands (£8) unlocks banded clams, banded glute bridges, banded lateral walks, and banded pull-aparts for upper back — all high-value postpartum movements.

## PHASE 3 — Build Capacity (Weeks 5–7)

Now we build genuine strength. She's ~10–12 weeks postpartum, ideally with a pelvic floor physio consult behind her. Real loading begins.

### Week 5 — Structured upper/lower split

**MONDAY — Lower body strength**

| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Tempo | Progression variable |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bodyweight squat, full depth | 4 × 12 | 3-1-1-1 | Depth, then tempo (add 1s to eccentric) |
| Reverse lunge | 3 × 8 each | 2-1-1 | Reps, then range, then load |
| Single-leg glute bridge | 3 × 10 each | 2-2-1 | Reps to 12 |
| Side-lying hip abduction (top leg lift) | 3 × 12 each | 2-1-2 | Reps, then band |
| Calf raise, double-leg | 3 × 15 | 2-1-2 | Move to single-leg |

**WEDNESDAY — Upper body & core strength**

| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Tempo | Progression variable |
|---|---|---|---|
| Incline push-up (bench/sofa height) | 4 × 8 | 3-1-1 | Lower the incline over weeks |
| Prone Y-T-W raises | 3 × 8 each | 2-2-2 | Reps to 12 |
| Superman hold | 3 × 20s | Isometric | Time |
| Dead bug, full | 3 × 8 each | 3-1-3 | Reps to 10 |
| Side plank from knees | 3 × 20s each | Isometric | Time, then move to full |
| Bird-dog | 3 × 10 each | 2-2-2 | Add pulse at end range |

**FRIDAY — Full body**

Circuit of 3 rounds, quality over speed:
- Goblet-style squat (hold a rolled towel/book at chest) — 12 reps, 3s eccentric
- Push-up at chosen incline — 8 reps
- Reverse lunge — 8 each
- Wall sit — 30s
- Bird-dog — 8 each

### Week 6 — Progressive overload week

Same structure. Apply one of these to each exercise:
- +2 reps, OR
- +1 second on eccentric or hold, OR
- Lower the incline (push-ups) / go deeper (squats)

Do not add on every variable at once. Pick one per lift.

### Week 7 — Introduce unilateral emphasis and load

**Structural changes:**

- **Bulgarian split squat** (rear foot on sofa or low bench) replaces reverse lunge, 3 × 8 each. This is a big step up — unilateral, deeper stretch, high glute demand.
- **Push-up progression check**: If she can do 3 × 10 at sofa height cleanly, move to knee push-ups on the floor, 3 × 6–8. If not, stay put and add reps.
- **Side plank progression**: Move from knees to full side plank, 3 × 15s each side.
- **Introduce hip hinge pattern**: **Single-leg RDL, bodyweight**, 3 × 8 each. Slow. Focus on control, not depth. Use a wall for fingertip balance if needed.

**Load introduction (if equipment available):**

This is the safest window to introduce external load — she has 3+ weeks of clean bodyweight strength work, DRA is progressing, pelvic floor is being reassessed.

- **Goblet squat with a dumbbell** (5–8 kg) — 3 × 10, replacing bodyweight squat
- **Dumbbell RDL** (2 × 5 kg) — 3 × 8, replaces or supplements bodyweight version
- **Dumbbell row, single arm** (5–8 kg, hand on sofa for support) — 3 × 8 each. This is a big-value addition for postpartum upper back and posture.
- **Suitcase carry** — walk 20 m holding a dumbbell in one hand, 3 × each side. Great for anti-lateral-flexion core work without any crunching.

## Progression Tracking Framework

Give her a simple training log. Each session records:

1. **Load** (bodyweight variation or dumbbell weight)
2. **Sets × reps completed**
3. **Tempo** used (especially eccentric)
4. **RPE** (rate of perceived exertion 1–10) — target 6–7 through Weeks 3–7, meaning "could do 3–4 more reps if pushed"
5. **Any red flags** — doming, leaking, scar sensations, pelvic heaviness

**Rule for progression:** Only progress a lift when she can complete all prescribed sets at the top of the rep range, at the prescribed tempo, with RPE ≤7, and zero red flags for **two consecutive sessions**. This is deliberately slow — postpartum tissue remodelling rewards patience.

# Progressive Core Reintroduction Protocol

Full clearance opens the door to real core work, but "cleared for exercise" ≠ "cleared to crunch." The C-section severed and reconnected multiple abdominal layers (skin, fat, fascia, rectus separation, peritoneum, uterus) and the linea alba has spent nine months stretched. Rushing core loading now is the single most common way postpartum women end up with persistent DRA, back pain, or pelvic floor issues at Month 6.

We rebuild in a specific order: **breath → deep core → anti-movement → anti-rotation → dynamic → loaded → flexion (last, if at all).**

---

## Prerequisite: The DRA Self-Check

Before ANY progression beyond what she's already doing, run this on Wednesday.

**Test:**
1. Lying on back, knees bent, feet flat
2. Fingers flat across midline just above the navel
3. Lift head and shoulders slightly off the mat (mini-crunch)
4. Feel across the linea alba: above navel, at navel, below navel
5. Note: **gap width in finger-widths** AND **tension quality** (firm, soft, or squishy/no floor)

**Interpretation:**

| Finding | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| <2 fingers, firm tension | Functionally closed | Progress through the protocol below normally |
| 2–3 fingers, firm tension | Moderate gap, good function | Progress but slower — spend 2 weeks per stage |
| Any width, soft/squishy (no floor) | Poor connective tissue tension | Stay at Stage 1–2 only; pelvic floor physio referral is essential |
| >3 fingers regardless of tension | Significant DRA | Stage 1 only; refer to physio before any progression |

**Also watch for:**
- **Doming** — the midline pushes UP into a ridge during effort
- **Coning** — the midline pulls DOWN into a valley
- Either = the load exceeds current capacity. Regress.

Retest every 2 weeks through the programme.

---

## Stage 1 — Foundation (Where She Is Now)

**Timing:** She's been doing this since Week 1. Continues throughout the programme as a warm-up.

- Diaphragmatic breathing
- Pelvic floor contractions (integrated with exhale)
- Heel slides
- Pelvic tilts
- Supine march
- Glute bridge with exhale

**What she's training:** The 360° breath-brace pattern. Pelvic floor and transverse abdominis coordination. This is the foundation everything else sits on. Even in Week 12, she should still be doing 5 minutes of this as a warm-up.

---

## Stage 2 — Anti-Extension (Weeks 3–4 of Programme)

**Goal:** Resist the spine arching under load. Trains deep core to hold neutral against gravity.

She's already doing dead bug and bird-dog. Progressions:

**Week 3:**
- Dead bug, heel-tap version — 3 × 6 each side, exhale on the tap
- Bird-dog, single-limb (arm OR leg, not both) — 3 × 6 each, 3s hold

**Week 4:**
- Dead bug, full opposite arm/leg — 3 × 6 each side, slow tempo
- Bird-dog, full opposite arm/leg — 3 × 6 each, 3s hold at extension

**Cues:**
- Exhale as the limb extends
- Ribs stay down (no flaring)
- Lower back stays glued to the mat during dead bug
- No doming — check by glancing at midline during reps

**Red flag:** If she can't keep lower back flat during dead bug, regress to heel-tap only for another week.

---

## Stage 3 — Anti-Lateral-Flexion (Weeks 5–6)

**Goal:** Resist sideways collapse. Trains obliques and quadratus lumborum without spinal flexion.

**Week 5:**
- **Side plank from knees** — 3 × 15s each side. Hips stacked, straight line from knee to shoulder.
- **Glute bridge march** — 3 × 6 each leg. Bridge up, march one knee toward chest without letting the hips drop. Massive anti-rotation and anti-lateral bonus.
- Continue dead bug and bird-dog from Stage 2, progressing reps.

**Week 6:**
- Side plank from knees — 3 × 20s each side
- **Suitcase carry** (if she has a dumbbell or a heavy handbag) — 3 × 20m each side. Hold weight in one hand, walk tall, don't let the shoulder drop. This is genuinely excellent postpartum core work.
- **Bird-dog with pulse** — 3 × 8 each, small pulse at end range for 3 reps

**Cues:**
- Ribs stack over hips, hips stack over knees on side plank
- No sagging through the waist
- Breathe throughout the hold — no breath-holding

---

## Stage 4 — Anti-Rotation (Week 7)

**Goal:** Resist twisting forces. This is where obliques and deep core coordinate under real demand.

**Week 7:**
- **Pallof press** (band anchored to a door hinge at chest height) — 3 × 8 each side. Press band straight out from chest, resist the pull to rotate. If no band, use standing anti-rotation with a light weight held at chest.
- **Bird-dog with knee-to-elbow** — 3 × 6 each side. From bird-dog extension, bring opposite elbow and knee together under the torso without rotating.
- **Standing chop** with light weight or band — 3 × 8 each direction. Move weight diagonally across body with no twisting through torso.
- Continue side plank progressions.

**Cues:**
- Hips face forward throughout
- The core stops rotation — nothing else
- Slow tempo, especially in the return phase

---

## Stage 5 — Full Side Plank & Dynamic Anti-Movement (Week 8)

**Prerequisite:** Clean 20s side plank from knees, no waist sag, no leaking, no doming.

- **Full side plank** — 3 × 15s each side, building to 30s over Weeks 8–9
- **Side plank with hip dip** — introduced Week 10 as originally scripted, 3 × 8 each
- **Dead bug with band pull-over** (band anchored behind her head, held in extended arms) — 3 × 8 each side. Real load on the anti-extension pattern.
- **Farmer's carry** (both hands loaded) — 3 × 30m
- **Pallof press with hold** — 3 × 8 each side, 3s hold at full extension

---

## Stage 6 — Hollow Positions (Weeks 8–10)

**Goal:** Full anterior core loading in a lengthened position. This is where we start approaching what most people think of as "abs work."

**Prerequisites:** DRA <2 fingers with firm tension, no doming during dead bug or side plank at any point.

**Week 8:**
- **Hollow hold, bent-knee** — 3 × 15s. Lower back pressed into mat, knees bent, arms by sides. Check midline for doming.
- If doming appears, regress to dead bug for another 2 weeks.

**Week 9:**
- Hollow hold, bent-knee — 3 × 20s
- **Hollow hold with one leg extended** — 3 × 15s (alternating)

**Week 10:**
- Hollow hold, full (legs straight, arms overhead) — 3 × 15s **only if no doming**
- Otherwise stay at bent-knee variation

**Cues:**
- Lower back cemented to the floor throughout
- If the lower back lifts, the load is too high — bend the knees more or lower the arms
- Exhale steadily throughout, no breath-holding
- Watch the midline every single rep

---

## Stage 7 — Spinal Flexion (Week 10+ IF appropriate)

**This is the last thing we add, and only if warranted.**

Spinal flexion (crunches, sit-ups, V-ups, toes-to-bar, most "ab" work) puts maximum tensile stress on the linea alba. For many postpartum women, this movement pattern is fine after DRA is functionally closed. For others, it should be avoided permanently in favour of anti-movement patterns.

**Prerequisites for introducing flexion:**
1. DRA <1 finger with firm tension (retested)
2. Zero doming or coning in ANY movement across the last 4 weeks
3. Full 30s side plank on both sides
4. Full hollow hold 20s with no midline change
5. No leaking, heaviness, or scar pain in any session
6. Ideally, pelvic health physio has cleared her for flexion work

**Week 10 or later (only if all above pass):**
- **Modified crunch** — 3 × 8, small range of motion, exhale forcefully on the way up, watch midline in a mirror
- If ANY doming: stop immediately, this movement is not appropriate yet (or possibly ever, and that's fine — plenty of strong athletes never train flexion)

**Honest note:** Anti-extension, anti-rotation, and anti-lateral-flexion patterns build stronger, more functional cores than crunches for essentially everyone, postpartum or not. There is no compelling reason to prioritise flexion. If she wants defined abs, that's a body composition question (nutrition + training + genetics), not a crunch question.

---

## Movements to AVOID Until Explicitly Cleared

Regardless of how she progresses, these are on the no-list at least through end of programme:

- Sit-ups and crunches to full range
- V-ups, toe-touches, jack-knives
- Russian twists with rotation and load
- Full sit-up variants (butterfly, decline, weighted)
- Straight-leg raises from lying (huge lower-back and linea alba stress)
- Toes-to-bar, hanging leg raises
- Full planks before 30s side plank on both sides
- Mountain climbers at speed
- Any "ab burner" style circuit with high reps and no breath control

Most of these can be reassessed at 6 months postpartum with a pelvic health physio.

---

## Warning Signs During Any Core Session

Stop immediately and regress if she experiences:

- **Doming or coning** at the midline
- **Leaking** urine or stool
- **Pelvic heaviness** or a "dragging" sensation
- **Scar tugging, pulling, or pain**
- **Bulging** at the linea alba during effort
- **Lower back pain** during or after
- **Held breath** — this indicates the load is exceeding her capacity to brace

Any single one of these = regress one stage and hold for a week. Multiple signs = back to Stage 1–2 and physio referral.

---

## Weekly Core Volume Guide

She doesn't need dedicated "core days." Core work is embedded into every session as it already is in the programme.

- **Weeks 3–4:** 5–8 min of core work per session, embedded
- **Weeks 5–7:** 8–10 min per session
- **Weeks 8–10:** 10–12 min per session
- **Weeks 11–12:** 10–15 min per session

More is not better. Quality of contraction and clean movement patterns matter far more than volume. A perfectly executed 3 × 8 dead bug beats a sloppy 3 × 20 every time.

- **End of Week 8:** DRA + assess readiness for hollow work

Log everything. If DRA isn't closing by Week 8, that's a signal to escalate to pelvic health physio, not to train harder.

- **Hollow hold with one leg extended** — 3 × 15s alternating

- Farmer's carry (both hands loaded) — 3 × 30m

- Push-up
- Reverse lunge, alternating
- Bird-dog

1. Single-leg stand 30s each side, no wobble
2. Single-leg squat to 45° depth × 10 each, no leaking or heaviness
3. Single-leg heel raise × 20 each side
4. 30 min brisk walk with no leaking, heaviness, or scar sensations
5. Forceful cough and forceful exhale — no leaking
6. Jog on the spot 60s — no leaking, heaviness, doming, or scar pain

**Ideally reviewed by pelvic health physio before pass is confirmed.**

**MON — Lower**
- Tempo squat 3-1-1 — 3 × 10
- Reverse lunge with slow knee drive — 3 × 8 each
- Step-up with pause at top — 3 × 8 each
- Single-leg RDL — 3 × 8 each
- Side plank with hip dip — 3 × 8 each

**WED — Upper/core**
- Full push-up (or best progression) — 3 × 8
- Pike push-up — 3 × 8
- Full side plank — 3 × 25s each

- Farmer's carry — 3 × 40m

- Single-leg RDL — 3 × 8 each (loaded if possible)
- **Squat jumps 3 × 6** — ONLY if Week 10 impact screen passed AND pogo hops were symptom-free. Otherwise, tempo squat 3 × 12.
- Glute bridge march — 3 × 10 each
- Side-lying abduction — 3 × 15 each

**TUES** — Walk 45–60 min briskly, include short pace pickups (no jogging yet)

**WED — Upper/core**
- Full push-up — 4 × max quality reps
- Pike push-up — 3 × 8
- Full side plank — 3 × 30s each
- Dead bug — 3 × 10 each
- Hollow hold — 3 × 20s
- Bird-dog — 3 × 10 each
- Farmer's carry — 3 × 40m

**THURS** — Walk + mobility

**FRI — Conditioning circuit**
40s work / 20s rest, 4 rounds:
- Squat (loaded if available)
- Push-up
- Reverse lunge
- Mountain climbers, slow (regress to bird-dog if doming)
- Side plank

**SAT — Cardio session**

**If cleared for jogging** (Week 10 impact screen + pogo hops + Week 11 squat jumps all symptom-free): 4 min walk / 1 min slow jog × 4.

**If not cleared:** Brisk hill walking or 5 min brisk / 2 min recovery × 5.

### Week 12

**MON — Lower**
- Bulgarian split squat — 4 × 10 each
- Single-leg RDL — 4 × 10 each
- Squat jumps 3 × 8 (if cleared) OR tempo squat 4 × 12
- Glute bridge march — 3 × 12 each
- Step-up — 3 × 10 each

**WED — Upper/core**
- Full push-up — 4 × 8
- Pike push-up — 3 × 10
- Full side plank — 3 × 30s each
- Hollow hold — 3 × 25s
- Pallof press — 3 × 10 each with 3s hold
- **Modified crunch** — 3 × 8 ONLY IF all flexion prerequisites met (see below). Otherwise skip.
- Farmer's carry — 3 × 50m

- If cleared: 3 min walk / 2 min jog × 5
- If not cleared: continued brisk walking with hills or intervals

1. DRA <1 finger with firm tension
2. Zero doming or coning in any movement over the last 4 weeks
3. Full 30s side plank both sides
4. Full hollow hold 20s with no midline change
5. No leaking, heaviness, or scar pain
6. Ideally physio-cleared for flexion

If any prerequisite fails, skip crunches. Anti-movement patterns build better cores anyway.

# Consolidated 12-Week Postpartum Return Programme

**Client:** 33F, C-section, no complications. Started programme at 4 weeks postpartum. Cleared for moderate exercise at 6-week check with no jumping/impact for 4 additional weeks (impact restriction lifts end of programme Week 6). Breastfeeding. Training at home on a yoga mat, plus any equipment acquired along the way.

**Non-negotiable principles throughout:**
- Exhale on effort, no breath-holding
- Watch for doming, coning, leaking, heaviness, scar pain — stop immediately if any appear
- DRA reassessment every 2 weeks from Week 3 onwards
- Pelvic health physio referral is essential — ideally between Weeks 3–8, mandatory before any impact
- Progress via tempo, holds, leverage, and range before adding external load
- Never reduce protein below 1.8 g/kg while breastfeeding

---

## PHASE 1 — RECONNECT & RESTORE (Weeks 1–2)

*Light activity only. No abs, no heavy lifting, no impact.*

### Week 1

**Daily (all 7 days):** Diaphragmatic breathing, 2 × 10 breaths morning and evening. Lying supine, one hand on ribs, one on belly. Inhale wide into ribs, exhale slow through pursed lips with natural pelvic floor lift.

**Mon / Wed / Fri — 15 min sessions**
- Connection breathing — 2 × 10
- Pelvic floor: 2 × 10 slow (5s hold), 2 × 10 quick pulses
- Heel slides — 2 × 8 each leg
- Pelvic tilts — 2 × 10
- Glute squeezes supine — 2 × 10, 5s hold

**Tues / Thurs / Sat:** 20–30 min flat walk, conversational pace.

**Sun:** Rest or gentle walk.

**Scar mobilisation:** Once scar is fully healed and OB-cleared, 2–3 min daily light fingertip circles around (not on) scar.

### Week 2

**Mon / Wed / Fri sessions — 20 min**
- Breathing — 2 × 10
- Pelvic floor: 2 × 10 slow (5s hold), 2 × 10 quick pulses
- Heel slides — 2 × 10 each
- Pelvic tilts — 2 × 10
- Glute bridge — 3 × 10, 3s hold at top with full exhale
- Side-lying clam — 2 × 10 each, 2s hold
- Supine march — 2 × 8 each
- Cat-cow — 2 × 8
- Bird-dog, single-limb (arm OR leg) — 2 × 6 each

**Tues / Thurs / Sat:** 25–35 min flat walk.

**Sun:** Rest.

### Bridge Days (between 6-week appointment and Week 3 start)

Push tempo and holds within existing scope. Add wall push (3 × 10s holds) and shallow wall sit (2 × 15s). No new movement patterns. No training on appointment day.

---

## PHASE 2 — FOUNDATION (Weeks 3–4)

*Post-clearance. Structured strength begins.*

**DRA baseline test at start of Week 3.** Log gap width and tension quality.

### Week 3 — 4 sessions/week

**Mon / Wed / Fri — 25 min strength session**

Warm-up: cat-cow ×8, glute bridge ×10, world's greatest stretch ×3/side, breathing ×5

Circuit — 3 rounds:
1. Box squat to sofa height — 10 reps, 3s eccentric, 1s pause, 1s up
2. Wall push-up — 8 reps, 3s eccentric
3. Glute bridge — 12 reps, 3s hold at top
4. Bird-dog full (opposite arm/leg) — 6 each side, 3s hold at extension
5. Side-lying clam — 12 each, 2s hold
6. Dead bug, heel-tap version — 6 each side, slow
7. Standing single-leg balance — 30s each

**Tues / Thurs — walk 30–40 min + 10 min mobility**

**Sat — optional gentle mobility flow** (no deep twists, backbends, or planks)

**Sun — rest**

### Week 4

Same session structure, progressions:
- Squat: lower target to sofa arm/coffee table height
- Wall push-up: 3 × 10 (+2 reps)
- Glute bridge: progress to single-leg 3 × 6 each if double-leg feels easy
- Bird-dog: 3 × 8 each with 3s hold
- Dead bug: full opposite arm/leg version, 3 × 8 each
- Add: staggered stance balance holds, 3 × 20s each side

**DRA retest end of Week 4.**

**Equipment nudge:** Suggest mini-bands (~£8) — massive value for the next 8 weeks.

---

## PHASE 3 — BUILD CAPACITY (Weeks 5–7)

*~10–12 weeks postpartum. Real strength work begins. Still no impact.*

### Week 5 — Upper/lower split, 4 sessions

**MON — Lower body**
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Tempo |
|---|---|---|
| Bodyweight squat, full depth | 4 × 12 | 3-1-1-1 |
| Reverse lunge | 3 × 8 each | 2-1-1 |
| Single-leg glute bridge | 3 × 10 each | 2-2-1 |
| Side-lying hip abduction | 3 × 12 each | 2-1-2 |
| Calf raise, double-leg | 3 × 15 | 2-1-2 |

**TUES** — Walk 35–45 min

**WED — Upper body & core**
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Tempo |
|---|---|---|
| Incline push-up (bench/sofa height) | 4 × 8 | 3-1-1 |
| Prone Y-T-W raises | 3 × 8 each | 2-2-2 |
| Superman hold | 3 × 20s | iso |
| Dead bug, full | 3 × 8 each | 3-1-3 |
| Side plank from knees | 3 × 15s each | iso |
| Bird-dog | 3 × 10 each | 2-2-2 |
| Glute bridge march | 3 × 6 each | slow |

**THURS** — Walk + mobility

**FRI — Full body**
3 rounds, quality over speed:
- Goblet-hold squat (rolled towel/book at chest) — 12 reps, 3s eccentric
- Push-up at chosen incline — 8 reps
- Reverse lunge — 8 each
- Wall sit — 30s
- Bird-dog — 8 each

**SAT** — 45 min walk or gentle yoga
**SUN** — rest

### Week 6

Same structure. On each exercise, apply ONE progression: +2 reps, OR +1s eccentric/hold, OR lower incline / deeper range. Don't stack progressions.

**Side plank from knees:** 3 × 20s each
**Suitcase carry** (if she has dumbbell or heavy handbag) — 3 × 20m each side
**Bird-dog with pulse** — 3 × 8 each

**DRA retest end of Week 6. Assess readiness for anti-rotation work.**

### Week 7

Unilateral emphasis and load introduction.

**MON — Lower**
- Bulgarian split squat (rear foot on sofa/low bench) — 3 × 8 each
- Single-leg glute bridge — 3 × 10 each
- **Single-leg RDL, bodyweight** — 3 × 8 each, fingertip wall balance if needed
- Sumo squat — 3 × 12
- Single-leg calf raise — 3 × 8 each

**WED — Upper/core**
- Push-up progression: knee push-up on floor 3 × 6–8, OR sofa-height incline 3 × 10 if not yet ready
- Prone Y-T-W — 3 × 10 each
- Side plank from knees → progress toward full, 3 × 20s each
- Dead bug with arm extension — 3 × 8 each
- **Pallof press** (band anchored to door hinge) — 3 × 8 each side, OR standing anti-rotation with light weight
- **Bird-dog with knee-to-elbow** — 3 × 6 each
- Standing chop with light weight/band — 3 × 8 each direction

**FRI — Full body**
3 rounds:
- Goblet squat with dumbbell (5–8 kg if available) — 10 reps
- Push-up — 8 reps at current level
- Bulgarian split squat — 8 each
- Suitcase carry — 20m each side
- Bird-dog — 8 each

**Load introduction if equipment available:**
- Goblet squat with dumbbell replaces bodyweight squat
- Dumbbell RDL (2 × 5 kg) — 3 × 8
- Dumbbell single-arm row (5–8 kg, hand on sofa) — 3 × 8 each
- Suitcase carry with dumbbell — 3 × 20m each side

---

## PHASE 4 — STRENGTHEN & INTEGRATE (Weeks 8–10)

*~14 weeks postpartum. Impact restriction lifts partway through, but gated behind screening.*

**DRA retest at start of Week 8. Assess readiness for hollow work.**

### Week 8

**MON — Lower**
- Bulgarian split squat — 3 × 8 each (loaded if possible)
- Single-leg glute bridge — 3 × 10 each
- Sumo squat — 3 × 12
- Curtsy lunge — 3 × 8 each
- Single-leg calf raise — 3 × 10 each

**WED — Upper/core**
- Push-up, knees (or full if strong) — 3 × 6–8
- Pike push-up from knees — 2 × 6
- Full side plank — 3 × 15s each (build toward 30s)
- Dead bug with arm extension — 3 × 8 each
- Bird-dog with 2s pause — 3 × 8 each
- **Hollow hold, bent-knee** — 3 × 15s (regress to dead bug if any doming)
- **Dead bug with band pull-over** (if band available) — 3 × 8 each

**FRI — Conditioning circuit**
40s work / 20s rest, 3 rounds:
- Squat (loaded if possible)
- Push-up
- Reverse lunge, alternating
- Glute bridge
- Side plank

**Walks Tues/Thurs 40–50 min, Sat longer walk 50–60 min.**

### Week 9

**MON — Lower**
- Bulgarian split squat — 4 × 8 each
- **Step-up to sturdy surface** — 3 × 8 each, slow, driving through front heel
- Single-leg glute bridge — 3 × 10 each
- **Tempo squat 4-1-1** — 3 × 10, deep eccentric
- Side-lying abduction, banded — 3 × 15 each

**WED — Upper/core**
- Push-up progression — 3 × 8 at current level
- Pike push-up — 3 × 8
- Full side plank — 3 × 20s each
- **Hollow hold, bent-knee** — 3 × 20s
- **Hollow hold with one leg extended** — 3 × 15s alternating
- Pallof press with 3s hold — 3 × 8 each side
- Farmer's carry (both hands loaded) — 3 × 30m

**FRI — Low-impact conditioning circuit**
40s work / 20s rest, 4 rounds:
- Tempo squat (3s down, 1s up)
- Push-up
- Reverse lunge, alternating
- Bird-dog
- Side plank (alternate sides each round)

### Week 10 — Impact readiness screen

**Before ANY impact is introduced, she must pass all six:**
1. Single-leg stand 30s each side, no wobble
2. Single-leg squat to 45° depth × 10 each, no leaking or heaviness
3. Single-leg heel raise × 20 each side
4. 30 min brisk walk with no leaking, heaviness, or scar sensations
5. Forceful cough and forceful exhale — no leaking
6. Jog on the spot 60s — no leaking, heaviness, doming, or scar pain

**Ideally reviewed by pelvic health physio before pass is confirmed.**

**MON — Lower**
- Tempo squat 3-1-1 — 3 × 10
- Reverse lunge with slow knee drive — 3 × 8 each
- Step-up with pause at top — 3 × 8 each
- Single-leg RDL — 3 × 8 each
- Side plank with hip dip — 3 × 8 each

**WED — Upper/core**
- Full push-up (or best progression) — 3 × 8
- Pike push-up — 3 × 8
- Full side plank — 3 × 25s each
- **Hollow hold, full** (if no doming) — 3 × 15s
- Pallof press with hold — 3 × 8 each
- Farmer's carry — 3 × 40m

**FRI — Conditioning circuit** as Week 9, 4 rounds

**End of Week 10, if impact screen passed:** 2 × 20s low pogo hops, small quiet landings, monitor closely.

**If screen not passed:** Replace with 3 × 30s marching on the spot with high knees, no bounce. Refer to pelvic health physio urgently if not already seen.

**DRA retest end of Week 10. Assess readiness for spinal flexion work — only if <1 finger with firm tension AND zero doming across last 4 weeks.**

---

## PHASE 5 — RETURN TO PERFORMANCE (Weeks 11–12)

*~16–18 weeks postpartum. Consolidate strength, layer conditioning, prep for next chapter.*

### Week 11
